title: Micro-MAMA: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Multicore Prefetching
problem: Independent RL-based prefetchers on each core of a multicore system compete for shared memory bandwidth without coordination, causing each agent to greedily claim excessive bandwidth and converging to sub-optimal system-wide policies. This problem is an instance of the multi-agent credit assignment and non-stationarity challenge in MARL.
motivation: As core counts grow and memory bandwidth becomes increasingly shared, bandwidth-unaware per-core prefetchers degrade system throughput and fairness, motivating a coordinated multi-agent approach.
method: MAMA uses a two-tier architecture: distributed local multi-armed bandit agents on each core narrow the joint-action search space by selecting among local prefetch aggressiveness options, while a central supervisor agent with global bandwidth visibility learns joint policies that maximize system-wide throughput or fairness. Key local agents receive system-level perspective signals (estimated global bandwidth usage) to discourage actions that harm other cores. The supervisor uses a lightweight bandit over the local agents' reduced action space, avoiding the exponential joint-action blow-up of fully centralized control.
key_novelty: A hierarchical supervisor that provides global bandwidth perspective to local bandit prefetchers, enabling coordinated joint policies without requiring centralized control of all per-core decisions.
contributions: Identification of bandwidth competition as the core MARL failure mode for multicore RL prefetching
MAMA hierarchical architecture combining distributed local bandit agents with a global supervisor
2.1% average throughput improvement and 10.4% fairness improvement over independently operating agents on an 8-core system
Demonstration that gains increase further in bandwidth-constrained configurations

metrics.speedup: 2.1% throughput improvement over independent agents; 10.4% fairness improvement

baselines: independently operating per-core RL bandit prefetchers
limitations: Evaluation is on an 8-core simulated system; scalability to larger core counts and interaction with hardware prefetchers are not fully characterized.
primary_theme: Multi-agent RL for coordinated multicore prefetch policy learning
